walkStretches.blurb: The tram car rattles past arcade after arcade. Every one of these places takes in quarters all night, and every one of them pays somebody.
walkStretches.label: The arcade boards

lines.bw-bazaar: Shells, ashtrays, and WILDWOOD on everything. Cash only.
lines.bw-casino-arcadia: The biggest arcade on the boards. Bingo in the back, and the bingo is where the money is.
lines.bw-chapel: Hymns at night on the Boardwalk. A landmark: nobody shakes down a chapel.
lines.bw-eds-fun-arcade: Pinball, the claw, and a change girl who sees everything.
lines.bw-flashback: Dress up like a gangster, have your picture taken. The irony is not lost on anybody.
lines.bw-nutty-hut: Roasted peanuts and cashews by the scoop. The smell carries half a block.
lines.bw-old-macks: Thin crust, a line out the door, and the same three pizza men since the war.
lines.bw-olympia: Pokerino, skee-ball and a prize wall. The machines in the back pay out in cash, if you know to ask.
lines.bw-sportsland: Surreys and bikes by the hour. The kid at the counter knows every cop who rides the boards in the morning.
lines.bw-surfside: Bathing suits and beach towels. The owner pays his envelope on time.
lines.bw-taffy-tides: Salt water taffy pulled in the window. The tourists stand and watch.
lines.sb03: A family restaurant on the boards since anybody can remember. Chicken pot pie and a view of the ocean.

walkStretches.where: The Boardwalk, Rio Grande Avenue up to Andrews

walkStretches.blurb: The quieter end of the boards: fries in paper cones, a pancake house, ice cream at the Sea Shell. North Wildwood is Kessler country, and his people watch who walks it.
walkStretches.label: The North End boards

lines.bw-boat-tag: Little motor boats in a pool, kids bumping each other for a dime.
lines.bw-bobby-ds: A family fun center: skee-ball, the claw, a prize counter.
lines.bw-curlys: Fresh-cut fries in a paper cone, vinegar on the counter.
lines.bw-fudge-kitchenette: Fudge made in copper kettles while you watch. Boxes for the trip home.
lines.bw-gateway-25: An arcade at the 25th Avenue ramp, frozen custard at the window.
lines.bw-lil-nickys: Slices through a window, the boards' late-night pizza.
lines.bw-octopus-golf: Indoor mini golf under a giant octopus.
lines.bw-route-69: A diner with a car on the roof. Coffee all night.
lines.bw-sammys: Pancakes from six in the morning. The cops eat here, which is worth knowing.
lines.bw-sea-shell: Ice cream in a gingerbread cottage. The picnic tables fill up after dark.
lines.bw-skippers: Fried fish in a paper boat, a nautical rooftop, a line at lunch.
lines.sb01: A seafood house on the boards with a big neon sign. The owner is getting old and thinking about selling.

walkStretches.where: The Boardwalk in North Wildwood, 26th Avenue down to 16th

walkStretches.blurb: Neon from one end to the other: the clubs, the lounges, the saloons. The acts come down from Philadelphia and New York; so does the money. This is where a family shows it runs the town.
walkStretches.label: Pacific Avenue after dark

lines.pa-fairview: A neighborhood corner bar, the regulars on their own stools.
lines.pa-oasis: A corner nightclub with palm trees in neon.
lines.pa-quo-vadis: A cocktail lounge in turquoise and chrome.
lines.pa-rainbow: Rock and roll at the corner: the kids line up around the block.
lines.pa-riptide: Twin bands, a long bar, sailors on leave.
lines.pa-shore-comedy: A comedy club: two shows a night, a two-drink minimum.
lines.pa-starburst: Pizza at the window, the Neon arcade inside, the Starburst lounge on the corner and rooms upstairs.
lines.pa-stardust: A turquoise nightclub with a stage and a curtain.
lines.pa-uncle-vinnys: The comics who come down from New York play here.
lines.pa-wildwood-high: The high school. A public building: never for sale.
lines.pa01: A small, dark lounge. The bartender keeps a book.
lines.pa02: The velvet rope is real: the doorman decides who gets in.
lines.pa03: A club with a cigarette girl and a back door onto the alley.
lines.pa05: The supper club: a floor show, a dance band, and tables down front for the people who matter.
lines.sa05: A Victorian corner bar older than the town's charter. The back room has seen every deal on the island.
lines.sa08: Red sauce, candles in Chianti bottles, a private room upstairs.
lines.sa09: Hoagies, cold cuts and a phone the bookies use.
lines.sa20: Banjos, straw hats and beer by the pitcher. Packed every night in July.
lines.sb02: A marquee nightclub with headliners all summer.

walkStretches.where: Pacific Avenue, the club strip, Spicer Avenue to Burk

walkStretches.blurb: Fishing boats, ice houses, bait and fuel. Whatever comes onto the island by water comes in here, and the dock boss knows what is in every crate.
walkStretches.label: Otten's Harbor

lines.bay-urys: A waterfront restaurant at the foot of the causeway, boats at the rail.
lines.pk-ricks: Crabs, clams and shrimp to take out, benches out front. The fishermen eat here.
lines.pk-ship-shore: A bar on its own dock. The captains drink here, and so do the men who unload their boats.
lines.sb04: A restaurant on pilings over the bay: the boats tie up at the back door.

walkStretches.where: The bay docks, Park Boulevard and the harbor

walkStretches.blurb: New motels every season: boomerang roofs, kidney pools, pink doors. The builders need permits, concrete and labor, and every one of those can be sold to them.
walkStretches.label: The Crest motel strip

lines.at-ebb-tyde: A blue-hour motel with a blade sign over Atlantic Avenue.
lines.at-panorama: Motel apartments by the week, a sign in a row of colored tiles. Summer help packs four to a room.
lines.at-rio-grande-motel: Efficiency apartments in turquoise stucco. Cash for the season, no names in the book.
lines.at-satellite: A boomerang roof and a rocket on the sign: the newest thing in the Crest.
lines.at-schumanns: A family restaurant: the motel guests eat breakfast here.
lines.at-shore-motel: A small motel, clean and quiet. The owner wants to build a second floor.
lines.oc-beach-haus: Two stories around the pool, a beach ball on the sign.
lines.oc-star-lux: A modern motel with a pool pavilion and a starburst sign.
lines.sb05: An oceanfront resort with palm trees in neon. Families from Philadelphia book the same week every year.
lines.sb06: A motel built around its pool. Weekly rates, a manager who asks no questions.

walkStretches.where: Wildwood Crest: Ocean and Atlantic Avenues

walkStretches.blurb: Corner delis, churches, City Hall and the old lighthouse at the inlet. The year-round people live up here; so do the men who run the North End.
walkStretches.label: North Wildwood

lines.at-al-pizza: A corner pizza and deli. Delivery, which means a car that goes everywhere.
lines.at-bils: Pizza, steaks, hoagies, wings: the corner deli for the whole neighborhood.
lines.at-corner-inn: A corner hotel with a bar on the ground floor.
lines.at-romeos: A pizzeria at Taylor Avenue, new in town.
lines.club-avalon: The landmark nightclub of the North End. A place to be seen; never anybody's to own.
lines.hereford-light: The Hereford Inlet Light, 1874. A public landmark.
lines.nj-holy-redeemer: A stone church on New Jersey Avenue.
lines.nj-st-anselms: The parish church. Sunday mass is where the whole town sees who is with who.
lines.nw-city-hall: North Wildwood City Hall. The permits and the police are both here. Public: never for sale.
lines.nw-lollypop: A motel with a lollipop on the sign. Kids pick it from the car window.

walkStretches.where: Atlantic Avenue in North Wildwood, up to the Hereford Inlet
